lessons.title: You Are Living a Dream You Didn't Choose
lessons.key_idea: From childhood we are domesticated into thousands of beliefs, or agreements, that shape how we see ourselves and the world, and most of them we never chose.

lessons.title: Meet Your Inner Judge and Victim
lessons.key_idea: An inner Judge enforces our learned rules and an inner Victim carries the guilt and shame, punishing us again and again for the same mistake.

lessons.title: Be Impeccable with Your Word
lessons.key_idea: Your word has creative power, so speak with integrity, avoid gossip, and never use words against yourself or others.

lessons.title: Don't Take Anything Personally
lessons.key_idea: What others say and do reflects their own dream and beliefs, not the truth about you, so you don't have to carry it.

lessons.title: Don't Make Assumptions
lessons.key_idea: We invent stories about what others think and mean, then suffer over them, when asking clear questions and communicating openly would prevent the drama.

lessons.title: Always Do Your Best
lessons.key_idea: Your best changes from moment to moment, and simply doing your best, without over-pushing or holding back, keeps the inner Judge quiet and makes the other agreements possible.

lessons.title: Breaking Old Agreements, One Day at a Time
lessons.key_idea: Freedom comes from patiently replacing old fear-based agreements with the four new ones, forgiving yourself when you slip, and starting again.

plan.title: The Four Agreements
plan.author: Don Miguel Ruiz
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's structure and core teachings well, including domestication, the dream of the planet, the inner Judge and Victim, the four agreements, and the path to breaking old agreements.
plan.one_liner: Four simple promises to yourself that can free you from fear, drama and self-judgment.
plan.summary: Don Miguel Ruiz draws on ancient Toltec wisdom to explain why so many of us feel stuck in fear, guilt and self-judgment. He argues that from childhood we are domesticated. Parents, schools and society teach us thousands of beliefs, or agreements, about who we are and how the world works. We accept them without question, and an inner Judge and Victim enforce them, punishing us for falling short. Ruiz calls this shared reality the dream of the planet. To wake up, he offers four new agreements: be impeccable with your word, don't take anything personally, don't make assumptions, and always do your best. Each one targets a common source of suffering. Practised patiently, and forgiven when we slip, they help break old agreements and let us live with more freedom, honesty and love.
